uncited: This method computes the first step of the Tensor-Train (TT) decomposition by avoiding the explicit construction of the full mode-1 unfolded matrix.

It exploits the fact that the column space of the unfolded tensor is low-dimensional to compute the required right singular vectors via a subsampled SVD, thereby reducing memory usage and computational cost compared to standard SSVD.
- Input: A 4D tensor $\mathcal{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{N_1 \times N_2 \times N_3 \times N_4}$ and target TT ranks $R_1, R_2, R_3$.

- Output: The first TT core $C_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times N_1 \times R_1}$ and the intermediate matrix $V^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{R_1 \times (N_2 N_3 N_4)}$ which serves as the starting point for subsequent cores.
- $C_1$ is a matrix of shape $1 \times N_1 \times R_1$.
- $C_2$ is a 3D tensor of shape $R_1 \times N_2 \times R_2$.
- $C_3$ is a 3D tensor of shape $R_2 \times N_3 \times R_3$.
**Mode-1 Unfolding**: Unfold $\mathcal{T}$ into a matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N_1 \times (N_2 N_3 N_4)}$.
**Column Subsampling**: Recognize that $A$ is highly imbalanced with $N_1 \ll (N_2 N_3 N_4)$.
Typical values depend on the desired compression ratio and accuracy.
- **Imbalanced Matrix**: The matrix $A$ is highly imbalanced ($N_1 \ll N_2 N_3 N_4$), leading to linearly dependent columns.
- **Time Complexity**: Reduced compared to full SVD on $A$.
